text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall: SLO breach detected for streaming API (p99 > 2.5s) in eu-west-2. Spike started ~10:05 UTC. Alerts: tls_handshake_errors, connection_resets, nat_ephemeral_exhaustion. Dashboard: https://dash.internal/streams/eu-west-2?snapshot=3412349999

sresarah: On it. I'm on-call. Any service / customer reports?

dmitri: I'm seeing SNAT conntrack spikes and ephemeral port exhaustion on the NAT gateway in eu-west-2a -> large tail latency + TLS handshake timeouts. Metric snippets: ```sum(rate(nat_ephemeral_alloc_failures[5m])) by (az) = 420``` and `conntrack_count` jumped to 85% of table.

alex: Confirming streaming stalls correlate with TLS handshake spikes. p95 stayed OK-ish but p99 exploded due to retries/handshakes.

priya: Any recent deploys or config changes to client keepalive/connection reuse?

dmitri: No deploys in the last 3 hours. We're seeing a lot of short-lived connections from a couple of noisy customers plus cross-AZ hairpinning making NAT reuse worse.

engops: If ephemeral ports are exhausted we can scale NAT (request quota) or temporarily move traffic to another AZ. Can we fail traffic to eu-west-2b/2c?

sresarah: Quick mitigation plan: 1) throttle noisy clients via per-IP rate-limits, 2) route new streaming sessions from problematic AZ to other AZs, 3) enlarge conntrack table / ephemeral port range as a temporary patch.

dmitri: I'm patching conntrack/sysctl on the NAT hosts now. Running: ```sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=2000000``` and increasing ephemeral range: ```sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range='1024 65535'``` — applying to NAT fleet in eu-west-2a.

alex: I'm kicking a can to add an emergency routing rule to steer 30% of traffic to eu-west-2b LB pool: ```router update --traffic-split streams=70/30 --region eu-west-2```. Doing a canary first to 2b.

priya: Can we also enable `keepalive` and connection pooling on the gRPC frontends to reduce connection churn? That needs a restart of the edge frontend.

engops: Rolling restart of edge frontends in eu-west-2a scheduled, doing 10% at a time. Command: ```kubectl -n edge rollout restart deploy/streams-edge --selector=az=eu-west-2a```

sresarah: Noted. I'll coordinate customer comms after we see initial metrics.

support-ollie: We have 4 support tickets from high-traffic customers reporting stalls; one customer (AcmeChat) is showing streaming timeouts on their dashboards. Need an advisory.

product-jamie: Drafting a short message: "We're currently mitigating increased streaming latency in eu-west-2 caused by NAT connection exhaustion leading to TLS handshakes timing out. We've applied traffic rerouting and increased conntrack capacity; some customers may see intermittent disruptions. We'll update in 30 minutes with status and timeline." Thoughts?

alex: Sounds good. Add 'no data leakage' & 'we prioritize restoring connectivity' line.

incident-bot: Action items assigned: @dmitri (NAT patch + monitor), @engops (traffic split), @priya (frontend keepalive + pool), @sresarah (customer comms). Pager escalations if p99 > 3s for another 15m.

sresarah: Update 10:18 UTC: conntrack max increased, ephemeral range widened, traffic split to 2b at 30%. Early metrics show tls_handshake_errors decreasing (~40% drop). p99 dropping but still above SLO.

dmitri: Packet loss analysis: we saw elevated retransmits between 2a->2a NAT path (hairpin) likely due to a misrouted VM causing extra hops. Opening a ticket with cloud provider for route flap.

engops: Temporary rule added to avoid hairpin route: `route-exclude --from=az:eu-west-2a --to=nat-host:hw2` — applied. Monitoring for impact.

support-ollie: AcmeChat updated: "We're seeing fewer timeouts now but still some stalls." They want ETA.

sresarah: ETA provisional: if current mitigations hold we'll be at normal p99 in 30-45m. I'll post a customer advisory now.

product-jamie: Customer advisory sent to affected customers and status page updated. Copy: "We experienced elevated streaming latency and occasional stalls in eu-west-2 due to NAT connection exhaustion and TLS handshake timeouts. We've applied routing and system-level mitigations; we're monitoring. No data compromise. Next update in 30m."

priya: After enabling keepalive and slight tuning of connection pool, connection churn reduced ~25% on the frontends. Logs show fewer `TLS_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT` entries.

incident-bot: Pager check: p99=2.1s (SLO 2.0s), p95=0.6s, streaming_stalls rate down 65% vs peak. Continue monitoring.

dmitri: Cloud provider acknowledged route flap and will remediate at infra layer; they also recommended long-term: provision NAT autoscaling or per-AZ NATs to eliminate cross-AZ hairpin.

engops: Filed CAPEX ask for per-AZ NAT pools and increasing ephemeral port quotas. Created ticket: NAT-2026-43.

sresarah: Handoff: I'm going to T+40 and will hand to morning oncall @dmitri in 20m. Please keep monitoring dashboards and escalate if p99 > 2.5s.

oncall-bot: Handoff scheduled: sresarah -> dmitri at 10:40 UTC. Reminder: include list of mitigations applied and customer contacts.

support-ollie: I'll keep AcmeChat and the other 3 customers updated.

product-jamie: I'll prepare a short post-incident note for the status page once we close.

last update 11:10 UTC: p99 back to 1.8s, streaming stalls down to baseline. Incident declared mitigated. Root cause likely NAT ephemeral port exhaustion exacerbated by cross-AZ hairpining + noisy client churn. Long-term actions: per-AZ NATs, NAT autoscale, connection pooling defaults tightened, and backlog of noisy-client rate-limits.

sresarah: Closing thread, will create postmortem and include timeline + customer impact table. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
